Some people throw away fridges because these break on their shelves. Don't toss it, fix it. The round pin you see in the picture is what holds the shelf support to the wall of the fridge. You have two options: 1) drill the pin with a 1/8 bit and then put a screw into that hold and pull the pin out. 2) Push the pin further into the support until it passes into the foam and remove the support. Option 1 is optimal as it causes no damage to the foam surrounding the fridge. To install, align the shelf support and push the round pin in until it is flush.

This was the ticket that allowed me to save a couple hundred dollars on a repairman.  It fit in my Fridgidaire Affinity dryer like a glove.

Electrolux EiMED55ii(W0) compatible.

Before calling a repair man for a probably $400 repair bill, I decided to use YouTube tutorials and disassemble the dryer myself.
We had Error Code 64 so I knew what it was narrowed down to by using the electrical breakout type paper that was stuffed inside the dryer behind the computer console. If you get Error 63, you will have to do all the same procedure here, but likely replace fuse instead of heater element.

When I got to the heater element I used a basic multimeter to test for "continuity" on all the fuses and terminals. They were all fine so when I detached the lines from the heater element and lifted it up pieces of the coils fells out. The coils were all burnt out.

This item replaced it perfectly and we are back in action.

Do use a shop vac to suck the dryer vent from outside and inside dryer hose to get all the piled lint out while you are doing all this maintenance.
